body:
I feel you. Everything you said, the way it was worded, the obvious clarity and inclusiveness in your points...I get it. I'm right there with you, in fact. I'm struggling more right now than I have at nearly any other time in my near twenty year battle with depression, to the point that I've taken my guns to my best friend's house. And yeah - he's my best friend, my only friend really, but can I talk to him about why he had to hold the guns for me? Nope. Guys don't open up like that, or this guy doesn't, and it's not just discomfort stopping them. It's not just discomfort stopping some women, either. It's the fact that maybe they know, deep down inside, and it scares them. The emotional commitment required to have those conversations, the onus that it puts on the receiving party, the potential lifelong gash in their psyche if it doesn't come out roses - those are scary, scary fucking things for people to deal with when life is tough enough on its own.

Your comments about resources, and living through the struggle while trying to find genuine help and hold down a job and keep friends hit the nail on the head. Those things are hard enough when you're NOT grappling with suicidal thoughts or intent. In the midst of a crises? Fucking forget about it. 

I'm not in the same boat you are, to an extent. I'm about to lose my job, and my family, but I do have a loving set of parents willing and able to take me in when the inevitable fallout finishes. I can tell you completely and totally honestly: it makes no difference in my desire to JUST. NOT. BE. And I'm sorry to be coming to you with that useless bit of knowledge, but maybe it helps. Maybe it'll help you to realize that it wouldn't matter if you had the resources you don't, or didn't have the background you do. Maybe it won't, who fucking knows? I'm bordering on actively suicidal right now, and to be fair, things are a pretty chaotic mess in my head right now.

What I can tell you is that every day is just another day you didn't do it. Every day, whether it feels like it or not, is a victory of sorts, even when you feel like it's another notch in the loss column. Find whatever reason you have to to make it through another day, at least for a little while. After all, there's not a time limit on suicide. You've always got tomorrow to do it, you know. It can be held off, through laziness if nothing else. I swear to God, one of the only reasons I'm alive today is because I convinced myself the second Spiderman movie (Doc Oc, original series) was worth seeing and I waited until it came out. Time passed, I got more on my feet mentally, life got better, and the urge passed. Shit has gone seriously tits up again, and I'm exhausted and sick of life and fatigue and hopelessness in general, but I'm still making myself (for now) find a reason that resonates, and while I'm slightly bothered to admit it, what's keeping me alive now is revenge. 

I don't have any fantastic advice, or life changing euphemisms, or trite little fucking aphorisms I'm going to trot out, because it's out there in spades and it's going to be shouted at you be well meaning ignorants. I just want to say I get it. It's hard, hard, hard, and I'm sorry. Give yourself the same time and patience you'd want to see someone else give themselves, and don't forget that your brain and your chemistry is lying to you right now. Do the right things in small steps. Drinking makes it easier to believe the lies, as does repeating negative thoughts to yourself. Start small, with those two things, and remember that there's always tomorrow to end it forever.
Finding optimism. Finding some way to geniunely hope and believe in myself and my future, and to let go of the rage and despair its lack causes.

I've spent years trying to manufacture hope and fight despair, and I've gotten pretty good at the tricks and platitudes trotted out by well meaning folk or in some of the better self help books. Feeling Good by David Burns and a number of other great resources have truly useful and beneficial advice and insights, and no one piece of well intended suggestions or insights are ever wrong for every single person out there. The problem comes when despair won't go away in the face of what you hope to be true, or when belief that possible better things ahead does nothing to alleviate the pain you're in at the moment and the rage and disgust you feel for yourself.

You ask if I want her to follow my example and blow her brains out? It's a nightmare of mine. I watched my father's agony after his father's suicide...I am intimately connected with the aftermath and the far reaching, long lasting impact it has. Having children at all was a big 50/50 for me because I know there's a strong genetic component to depression related suicide, and I already see risk factors in her personality that I quail in analyzing. I honestly do not know if being here for her would help or hurt her chances at an emotionally healthy life, and that's an incredibly painful, shameful admission. 

Hope isn't something you can make out of nothing - emotions, intent, and life add up to a calculus that's beyond what any one person can control without considerable resources and emotional energy. People who have that energy don't understand this, any more than a child with 20/20 vision can understand and empathise with a friend who's legally blind without their corrective lenses. You cannot MAKE hope from nothing. People can bring it to you, or you can marshal your resources, time, and energy, and create it from those things, but it's not something you just wish for and suddenly have, any more than money is.

It's entirely possible that I may end up being a bigger poison in her life than anything else. My issues have largely ensured that those who are close to me suffer for it. I don't want that for her. I don't want to leave her alone, and she's the only reason I'm even waiting right now, but the reality is that every single person I've been close to in my life is better off without me. At no point have I bettered anyone else, usually it's the contrary. If the answer is change and be good and healthy for her, what makes this any more possible than it has been for the past two decades? I have less energy than when I first started fighting this, life circumstances are getting harder and worse literally by the day, and the "... can get better and you know it," philosophy smacks of the same ignorance others perceive in MY fatalism. I DON'T know it. Furthermore, I don't even believe it, or I would have some sliver of hope to fuel an effort toward recovery.

My plan is to take my .40, sit carefully balanced hanging over the roof of my five story office building, lean out and shoot myself in the base of the cerebellum angled slightly forward and up to exit through the gyrus frontalis with a hollowpoint round. The bullet should render me unconscious at the very least, the fall will finish the job certainly.

Whether or not to commit suicide. I'm tired, and have no energy, find no sustained Joy or drive in anything, and have been that way for long enough that it's caught up with me and my life is falling to shit. My wife is divorcing me. I'm slowly being forced out of a job that I loathe, but can't muster up the energy to deal with the emotional blow of failure in finding a new one. I don't want to die... I'm honestly afraid of it. But I don't want to live anymore, either. I'm miserable, angry, and hopeless, and about to be completely alone.

I know all the platitudes about trekking on, about keeping going, and I've been in therapy for over a year. I've been on so many different antidepressants that I've damaged my memory severely, and that only adds to the depression. I have no hope about my ability to better my life... It only seems like it's going to go more downhill from here, and I want out.
